{{nihongo|'''Uge Shrine'''|宇芸神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kōzuke Province]].

'''Uge Shrine''' (うげじんじゃ; {{ill|Kyūjitai|Q1147857|qid=Q1147857}}: 宇藝神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Kannari, {{ill|Tomioka, Gunma|Q873835|qid=Q873835}}, {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|Q129499|qid=Q129499}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and under the former {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=shrine ranking system}} it was a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}{{Sfn|Honda|1928|pp=817-819}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
* {{ill|Ukanomitama|de|Ukanomitama|eo|Ukanomitama|fr|Uka-no-Mitama|ja|ウカノミタマ|mni|ꯎꯀꯅꯣꯃꯤꯇꯃ|ru|Ука-но митама|simple|Ukanomitama|sv|Ukanomitama|th|อูกาโนมิตามะ|zh|宇迦之御魂神|qid=Q3080728|lt=Kura-inetama-no-Kami}} (うかのみたまのかみ){{Sfn|Honda|1928|pp=817-819}}<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|和書 |title=History of Tomioka City |date=1984-10-1 |year=1984 |publisher=Tomioka City |page=421 |doi=10.11501/9643274 |editor=Tomioka City History Editorial Committee |volume=Folklore volume}}{{要登録}}</ref>

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, it was founded in the Hakuhō era (late {{ill|7th century|Q8089|qid=Q8089}}), in the reign of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|Q335181|qid=Q335181}}{{Sfn|Honda|1928|pp=817-819}}. The present shrine site was originally where Akagi Shrine stood, and Uge Shrine was originally on the west side near Yoshida Pond{{Sfn|Honda|1928|pp=817-819}}<ref name=":0" />.

In the {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Engi}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as "Uge Shrine" in {{ill|Kanra District, Gunma|Q1076986|qid=Q1076986}}, {{ill|Kōzuke Province|Q1054838|qid=Q1054838}}, and is ranked as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}{{Sfn|Ozaki|1974|pp=40}}.

In the ''Kōzuke no Kuni Jinmyōchō'', both the {{ill|Nukisaki Shrine|Q10863796|qid=Q10863796|lt=Ichinomiya}} manuscript and the {{ill|Gunsho Ruijū|Q1554852|qid=Q1554852}} manuscript include "Junior First Rank, Ugi Daimyōjin" among the 12 guardian shrines of Kōzuke, and this is identified with this shrine<ref name=":0" />. On the other hand, the {{ill|Sōja Shrine (Maebashi)|Q17220813|qid=Q17220813|lt=Sōja}} manuscript does not include it among the 10 guardian shrines. In the Kanra District section, the Ichinomiya manuscript has "Junior First Rank, Ugi Daimyōjin," while the Gunsho Ruijū and Sōja manuscripts have "Junior First Rank, Sōgi Myōjin." {{ill|Kisao Ozaki|Q21698487|qid=Q21698487}} regarded the guardian-shrine entry and district entry as different shrines, assigning the latter to Soki Shrine (Soki, Tomioka){{Sfn|Ozaki|1974|pp=46,192-196}}.

It was destroyed by fire during the {{ill|Tenmei|Q1194121|qid=Q1194121}} era ({{ill|1781|Q7719|qid=Q7719}}-{{ill|1789|Q7772|qid=Q7772}}), and the current shrine buildings are said to have been rebuilt in April of {{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} 1 ({{ill|1716|Q6892|qid=Q6892}})<ref>{{ill|Kyōwa|Q960763|qid=Q960763}} 1 ({{ill|1801|Q6877|qid=Q6877}})?</ref>{{Sfn|Honda|1928|pp=817-819}}.

The festival date was November 3, but is now April 3 and October 15<ref name=":0" />.

=== Precincts ===
* Honden - one-bay {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}}.
* Haiden
* Mukuroji tree - 14 m tall, about 300 years old. Designated natural monument of Tomioka City.
* Precinct shrines<ref name=":0" />
** Akagi Shrine
** Takaokami Shrine
** Santai Shrine
** Shinmeigū
** Mishima Shrine
** Fuji Shrine
** Kotohira-gū
** Hokuto Shrine
** Ōikazuchi Shrine
